newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil accepts 339 mln real bid for B Band area 7.
newsitem.headline: Brazil accepts 339 mln real bid for B Band area 7.

text.p: A Canadian-led group won a concession to operate cellular services on the B Band frequency in central and western Brazil with a bid of 338.5 million reais, some 25.4 percent above the base price, an official said.
A Communications Ministry spokesman said the B Band privatization committee has accepted the lone bid for area 7 by the Americel consortium and granted the concession license.
"The commission has declared the bid accepted and granted the contract," the spokesman said.

The government had set a base price of 270 million reais ($252 million) for area 7, which covers the capital Brasilia as well as Acre, Goias, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul, Rondonia and Tocantins states.
The Americel consortium is made up of Bell Canada, a unit of BCE Inc, Telesystem Telecom Ltd, also of Canada, Citibank, and Brazil's Opportunity bank, and pension funds owned by Banco do Brasil.
It is the first concession to be granted of the 10 being offered across the country under Brazil's plan to privatize its mammoth telecommunications system.
Earlier Wednesday, the government announced the names of qualified bidders on the B Band concessions.
Five of the 15 groups that presented B Band bids in early April were declared unqualified and have five working days to appeal the ministry's decision.

The government had been expected to wait until after the appeals to declare winners for the first two concession areas but decided to proceed with the lone bid for area 7 because there was no competition, an official said.

The only other group that had been interested in the area seven concession was GFTT SA, a consortium made up of France Telecom, Brazilian telecom venture Teldin and private equity funds of Banco Garantia.
But a ministry spokesman said GFTT had pulled out of the running, so officials decided to move ahead and open Americel's bid.

Analysts said the reason for the light interest in area seven is that Telebras unit Telebrasilia has generally met demand for cellular service within Brasilia itself, while the surrounding regions are only sparsely populated.
